purpose: Dependency-free runtime observation rules. These independently authored rules produce evidence; they do not replace NUI design owners or release gates.

rules.description: An image element has a missing, empty, or explicit placeholder source that cannot represent a shippable asset by itself.
rules.falsifier: Framework evidence proves the source is injected before the element can render and the runtime observation resolves a real asset.

rules.description: A link-like element declares an empty navigation target, creating a control that communicates navigation without a destination.
rules.falsifier: The element is intentionally intercepted as an application command and exposes the correct semantic role and keyboard behavior.

rules.description: Material content appears authored to start fully invisible, making successful reading depend on a reveal path that must be proven at runtime.
rules.falsifier: Runtime evidence shows a reliable reveal path and content remains available when scripting, motion, or intersection observers are unavailable.

rules.description: An image element omits the alt attribute entirely, leaving its accessibility intent unspecified.
rules.falsifier: The rendered primitive supplies an equivalent accessible name through a framework abstraction and the source match is not the final semantic element.

rules.description: Focus outline styling is suppressed and requires evidence that an equally visible focus treatment replaces it.
rules.falsifier: The same interactive state has a clearly visible replacement focus indicator meeting the product accessibility contract.

rules.description: A page-level surface declares a large fixed minimum width that can force horizontal scrolling on smaller supported viewports.
rules.falsifier: The task is intentionally a fixed-size canvas/instrument or responsive runtime evidence shows the declaration is scoped away from smaller supported viewports.

rules.description: A content-bearing container combines clipping overflow with constrained dimensions, requiring proof that text and focusable descendants are not cut off.
rules.falsifier: Rendered geometry shows all required content and focus indicators remain reachable across the supported content and viewport matrix.

rules.description: A literal presentation color appears on an axis that a supplied design-system contract may declare token-owned.
rules.falsifier: The literal is part of the token definition itself, an approved data/brand value, or the active design contract does not own this axis.

rules.description: Repeated card-like containers are nested inside card-like parents, a structural convergence signal that may substitute containers for hierarchy.
rules.falsifier: The nested boundary expresses a real independent object, state, interaction or containment contract that spacing/dividers cannot represent truthfully.

rules.description: Text uses a clipped decorative gradient treatment, a convergence signal that should be justified by the selected visual thesis rather than applied reflexively.
rules.falsifier: The committed visual direction explicitly makes gradient material a semantic/signature mechanism and rendered critique confirms hierarchy and legibility remain strong.

rules.description: Repeated pill, badge, or chip-shaped treatments accumulate without explicit state, category, filter, metadata, or interaction semantics, a convergence signal that may substitute decoration for hierarchy.
rules.falsifier: Each repeated treatment consistently represents an explicit state, category, filter, metadata, or interaction contract and rendered critique shows the shape improves scanning or operability rather than decorating equivalently weighted content.

rules.description: Repeated small all-caps presentation labels accumulate as simulated sophistication without clear metadata, identifier, state, or hierarchy necessity.
rules.falsifier: The labels are genuine identifiers, metadata, states, or a typography contract explicitly requires the treatment and rendered evidence proves role separation and legibility remain strong.

rules.description: Many sibling card, panel, or surface boundaries use equivalent containment, a structural convergence signal that may replace authored hierarchy and grouping with repeated shells.
rules.falsifier: Each repeated boundary maps to an independent object, state, interaction, or containment contract and alternative grouping would reduce product truth, comprehension, or operability.

rules.description: The observed surface emitted an uncaught runtime or console error during the inspected state.
rules.falsifier: A repeat observation on the same revision/state proves the message came from unrelated tooling or a non-product source and the product runtime is clean.

rules.description: The rendered document is wider than its client viewport, producing page-level horizontal overflow that requires an explicit interaction/layout justification.
rules.falsifier: The surface is an intentionally pannable fixed canvas/instrument or a re-observation proves horizontal overflow is confined to an explicit operable sub-surface rather than the document.

rules.description: Driver hit-testing reports essential visible text as covered by another rendered element in the inspected state.
rules.falsifier: The covered text is intentionally non-essential/duplicate or re-observation shows the hit-test/occlusion report was incorrect for the same revision and state.
